description: A team of space enthusiasts, researchers, and tech explorers mapping Earth for the Moon and Mars.
summary:
Before we can send rovers or astronauts to the Moon and Mars, we have to test our gear in the most similar places on Earth. Finding those terrestrial twins usually means sifting through disconnected datasets. To solve this, we built Asterris.
Asterris is an end-to-end planetary analog discovery and mission engineering web app. It tackles the challenge by combining interactive 3D terrain visualization with a custom scientific engine that evaluates surface DEMs, spectral signatures, seasonal shifts, and subsurface data. Users can explore planetary targets, run ML-backed clustering and similarity algorithms to pinpoint matching Earth analog sites, and stress-test rover traversal and drilling operations through built-in physics simulations.
By bringing discovery, scientific comparison, and field campaign optimization under one roof, Asterris cuts down mission planning time and helps teams de-risk space exploration right here on Earth.
details:
What it does & how it works:

Asterris is an end-to-end planetary analog discovery and mission engineering platform. When planning missions to the Moon or Mars, scientists need "terrestrial twins"—places on Earth with similar geology, terrain, and subsurface conditions to test rovers and drills. Instead of manually cross-referencing scattered datasets, Asterris unifies this workflow into six connected modules: Mission Control, Planetary Explorer, Analog Discovery Lab, Scientific Comparison, Mission Engineering, and Field Campaign Reports.

Under the hood, our custom scientific engine analyzes Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) for slope and roughness, spectral signatures for mineral composition, seasonal variations, and subsurface stratigraphy (radar/GPR profiles and ice-table depth). Using machine learning clustering and multi-dimensional similarity scoring, it ranks Earth analog sites against extraterrestrial targets. Once a site is selected, users can run physics-based rover traversal and drilling simulations to see how hardware performs on that specific terrain before generating a field campaign report.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Space hardware testing is costly, and choosing the wrong test site on Earth can lead to mission failure in space. Asterris cuts down research time from weeks to minutes, eliminates guesswork with explainable similarity breakdowns, and democratizes mission planning by giving students, researchers, and engineers access to an integrated planetary workbench. Its intended impact is to de-risk future Lunar and Martian exploration by making Earth-based field validation faster, more accurate, and grounded in multi-modal data.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software:

Languages: Python, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3

Frameworks & Libraries: Streamlit (UI & state management), Three.js & GLTFLoader (3D planetary globes and terrain meshes), Plotly (scientific charting), NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, and Scikit-learn (clustering, DEM analysis, and similarity algorithms)

Deployment & Dev Tools: Docker, Docker Compose, Git, and Pytest for automated validation

Creativity & Team Considerations:

Most geospatial tools stop at 2D maps or surface-level comparisons. We took a creative leap by combining surface terrain, subsurface modeling, and hardware physics simulations in a single dark-themed, mission-control interface. While building Asterris, our team carefully considered:

1. Scientific Rigor & Explainability: Rather than giving a "black-box" match score, we designed our engine to explain why an Earth site matches a Mars or Moon target across topography, mineralogy, and subsurface layers.

2. Real-World Constraints: We factored in logistics, seasonal windows, and hardware limits (like drill thermal loads and rover slip on steep slopes).

3. Reliability: We engineered graceful fallbacks between live Earth observation APIs and our curated seed catalogs so the app remains fast and functional even offline.
